title: A Deep Discount Denied Until the Expansion Was Signed
scenario_text:
A deal desk analyst at Larchwood Media must decide whether to grant a 28% discount on a new deal, given how a comparable request was handled earlier this year.

**Decision A (2024-03-19)**
Customer 'Piedmont Labs' requested a 28% discount. DENIED. Note: 'Discounts above 15% require a verified, countersigned multi-year expansion commitment. Piedmont provided only a verbal forecast of future growth — nothing signed. Capped at 15%.'

**Current request C (2024-09-30)**
Customer 'Calder Group' requests the same 28% discount. Calder has attached a countersigned 3-year expansion order committing to additional seats worth $900K in incremental ARR. The order is executed by both parties and verified by Deal Desk.

**Discount Authority Policy (current, unchanged this year)**
Deal Desk may grant discounts up to 30% when the deal includes a verified, countersigned multi-year expansion commitment of at least $500K incremental ARR. Without such a commitment, the discount cap is 15%. The verified-commitment requirement and the 30% ceiling have not changed this year.

**Slack — #deal-desk**
AE: 'We denied a 28% ask for Piedmont back in March, so Calder should get capped at 15% too — let's be consistent.'
Analyst: 'Piedmont was denied because nothing was signed. Calder has a countersigned expansion order attached. That's new information — let me line it up against the policy.'

The Piedmont denial rested on the absence of a signed commitment. Calder's countersigned order clears the $500K incremental-ARR bar.
question: How should the analyst handle Calder Group's 28% discount request?
choices: Cap Calder at 15%, consistent with the March denial of a similar 28% request for Piedmont.

Approve the 28% discount: Calder has a verified, countersigned expansion order worth $900K incremental ARR, which satisfies the exact condition Piedmont lacked, so the deeper discount is authorized under the unchanged policy.
Escalate the discount to VP Sales, since any discount above 15% is inherently outside Deal Desk authority.
Offer a 21% discount as a midpoint between the 15% cap and the requested 28%.
